construction_markdown:
No new leaderboard code is submitted. I audit the following strict uniform-repetition variant of AG–affine alphabet reduction.

For `m≥2` and `rho≥1`, put `q=2^m`. Let `X/F_q` be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve, let `D=P_1+...+P_L` consist of distinct rational points, and let `G` be an `F_q`-rational divisor of degree `a<L`, disjoint from `D`. Use the functional AG outer code `C_L(D,G)` of dimension `K=l(G)`. Encode each field symbol using `2^rho` identical copies of the affine encoder

`H_m:F_q→RM(1,m−1)=[2^(m−1),m,2^(m−2)]_2`.

No padding, shortening, or puncturing is used. Exact target length and product-certified distance force

`L=2^(31−m−rho)`, `a≤A=2^(22−m−rho)`.

A finite Castelnuovo–Ihara sieve proves `mK≤2706` throughout this family. More sharply, every instance with `m≥10` has `mK≤975`, so strict repetition cannot repair any of the `m=10,...,16` AG–affine gateways or improve the accepted dimension-1040 code there. Any repeated-inner improvement must use `m≤9`. The largest surviving parameter upper bound is `m=3`, `rho=1`, `K≤902`, hence conditional dimension at most 2706; no curve or divisor realizing it is supplied.

If `r=l(G)−1`, removing the fixed part and factoring the complete-series map with degree `delta` gives the necessary condition `L≤delta U_q(pi(floor(A/delta),r))`. Exact enumeration proves global binary dimension at most 2706.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Intended recipients: algebraic literature and bottleneck positions. The extremal surviving repeated case is over `F_8`: it would require `L=2^27` rational points and a divisor of degree at most `2^18` with `l(G)=902`. The complete series is necessarily birational, has moving degree between 262020 and 262144, and forces genus between 26843544 and 38046213. Can an explicit finite small-field point bound, Frobenius-angle LP certificate, or classification of such near-Castelnuovo series exclude this gateway?

distance_audit: The repeated affine inner code has exact parameters `[2^(m−1+rho),m,2^(m−2+rho)]_2`.
The standard outer AG distance is at least `L−a`; thus product distance is at least `(L−a)2^(m−2+rho)`. Requiring this to be at least `511·2^20` is exactly `a≤2^(22−m−rho)=L/512`.
For the extremal surviving ledger `(m,rho,L,A,K)=(3,1,2^27,2^18,902)`, a hypothetical final code would have dimension `3·902=2706`; the distance certificate at `a=A` is `(2^27−2^18)·4=535,822,336`.
No curve, divisor, point ordering, or Riemann–Roch basis realizing a surviving row is supplied, so `minimum_distance`, `dimension`, and `rate` remain null.
explicitness_audit: The obstruction uses only exact integer loops over the displayed finite ranges; it does not select a generator matrix and does not use randomness, conditional expectation, or exhaustive target-code search.

The audited family uses distinct rational evaluation points and exact unpadded length. Zero-padded non-power-of-two repetition factors, multiplicity AG codes, weighted inner maps, and non-product distance arguments are outside the theorem.
A qualifying instance would still have to specify the curve, all evaluation points, divisor, Riemann–Roch basis, field model, and their polynomial-time algorithms. None is supplied.
The workspace is read-only, so the lemma and posts are returned inline; no record, proof file, validator run, or dashboard build was produced.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Conditional template only: given an explicit field model, curve, ordered rational points, divisor, and ordered Riemann–Roch basis `f_1,...,f_K`, index binary rows by `(j,i)` with `1≤j≤K` and `0≤i<m`. Evaluate `alpha^i f_j(P_t)` for every outer point, apply the fixed affine truth-table encoder `H_m`, and emit `2^rho` consecutive copies of that inner block. No unconditional matrix is asserted because no surviving curve/divisor data are supplied.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: Conditional `O(kn·poly(log n))` bit operations, plus polynomial-time curve and Riemann–Roch preprocessing.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: There are exactly `kn=mK·L·2^(m−1+rho)` output bits. With polynomial-time field arithmetic, evaluation, and basis construction, each bit is computed using `poly(log n)` work; streaming all entries therefore costs `O(kn·poly(log n))≤n^{O(1)}`. This is only an explicitness-preserving reduction, not a construction claim.

obstructions: Every exact unpadded strict-repetition AG–affine product construction has binary dimension at most 2706, below the concrete GV reference dimension 2955.
Every such construction with alphabet degree `m≥10` has dimension at most 975 and therefore cannot improve the accepted k=1040 construction.
At `m=13`, one repetition lowers the exact sieve cap from the unrepeated conditional `k=1053` gateway to `k≤546`; further repetitions do not improve it.
The only rows not already below k=1040 occur for `m=2,...,9`; they still require enormous point-rich curves and suitable low-degree complete linear series, none of which is constructed.
This does not obstruct arbitrary AG concatenation, nonuniform or nonlinear alphabet reduction, zero-padded repetition factors, or distance proofs stronger than the ordinary product bound.

proof_markdown:
### Theorem

Fix `m≥2` and `rho≥1`. Consider a functional AG code over `F_q`, `q=2^m`, concatenated with `2^rho` identical copies of the affine inner encoder `RM(1,m−1)`, with exact unpadded binary length `2^30`. If distance is certified by the standard product bound, then the binary dimension is at most 2706. If `m≥10`, it is at most 975.

### Parameter reduction

The repeated inner code has length `2^(m−1+rho)`, dimension `m`, and distance `2^(m−2+rho)`. Therefore exact length gives

`L=2^(31−m−rho)`.

Writing `a=deg G`, the product certificate is

`(L−a)2^(m−2+rho)≥2^29−2^20`.

Substituting `L` shows this is equivalent to

`a≤A:=2^(22−m−rho)=L/512`. `(1)`

If `22−m−rho<0`, integrality gives `a≤0`, hence `K=l(G)≤1`. It remains to consider `1≤rho≤22−m`.

### Complete-linear-series sieve

Assume `K=l(G)≥3` and put `r=K−1`. A nonzero section replaces `G` by a linearly equivalent effective divisor. Remove the fixed part of its complete linear series. The resulting basepoint-free divisor has degree `a'≤A`, dimension `r`, and defines a morphism onto a nondegenerate curve in `P^r`.

Let `delta` be the degree onto the normalization of the image and `e` the image degree. Then `a'=delta e`, `e≥r`, and rational fibers contain at most `delta` points. Thus

`L≤delta·#Y(F_q)`.

For `e−1=s(r−1)+epsilon`, `0≤epsilon<r−1`, define

`pi(e,r)=s(s−1)(r−1)/2+s epsilon`.

Castelnuovo gives `g(Y)≤pi(e,r)`. Define the exact integer point bound

`U_q(h)=min(q+1+isqrt(4q)h, q+1+(isqrt((8q+1)h^2+4hq(q−1))−h)//2)`.

Monotonicity in degree and genus yields the necessary condition

`L≤delta U_q(pi(floor(A/delta),r))` `(2)`

for some

`1≤delta≤floor(A/r)`. `(3)`

### Exact finite enumeration

For each `m=2,...,16`, enumerate `rho=1,...,22−m`, `K=3,...,A+1`, and every `delta` in (3), retaining `K` only when (2) holds. All operations are integer additions, multiplications, divisions, and integer square roots. The resulting maxima are:

| `m` | maximizing `rho` | `K` cap | binary `mK` cap |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|2|1|1213|2426|
|3|1|902|2706|
|4|1|661|2644|
|5|1|479|2395|
|6|1|344|2064|
|7|1|246|1722|
|8|1|175|1400|
|9|1|124|1116|
|10|1|88|880|
|11|1|65|715|
|12|1|59|708|
|13|1|42|546|
|14|1,2,3|33|462|
|15|1|65|975|
|16|1|33|528|

For `m≥17`, (1) and `K≤a+1` give `mK≤m(2^(21−m)+1)` while the exponent is nonnegative, whose maximum is 289 at `m=17`; afterward `K≤1`. Thus the table is globally maximized by 2706, and its `m≥10` portion is maximized by 975.

### Extremal surviving row

At `(m,rho,K)=(3,1,902)`, one has

`q=8`, `L=134217728`, `A=262144`, `r=901`.

The exact loop gives

`max_(delta≥2) delta U_8(pi(floor(A/delta),901))=66941724<L`,

so the complete-series map must be birational. Moreover,

`U_8(pi(262019,901))=134217652<L`,

whereas

`U_8(pi(262020,901))=134218679≥L`.

Hence its moving degree must lie in `[262020,262144]`. Serre's bound gives

`g≥ceil((L−9)/5)=26843544`,

and Castelnuovo gives

`g≤pi(262144,901)=38046213`.

This is a concrete conditional geometry problem, not an existence or construction claim.

theorem_statement: For every exact-length, unpadded binary code obtained by concatenating a functional AG evaluation code `C_L(D,G)` over `F_(2^m)`, `m≥2`, with `2^rho` identical copies of `RM(1,m−1)`, `rho≥1`, when distance is certified by the standard product bound, the binary dimension is at most 2706. Every such instance with `m≥10` has dimension at most 975. Thus strict affine-inner repetition cannot improve the accepted k=1040 construction for any alphabet degree at least 10; any repeated-inner improvement must use `m≤9`.
title: Uniform inner repetition does not rescue AG–affine alphabet reduction
